title: release.yml: a job killed by timeout-minutes is reported as 'cancelled', so timeouts silently pass CI
body:
## Summary

A job killed by its own `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub Actions as **`cancelled`**, not **`failure`**. A workflow run whose only non-success job is cancelled inherits the run conclusion `cancelled` too — which on the runs list is visually indistinguishable from "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". It is grey, not red. It does not appear in the failed-runs filter and it sends no failure notification.

`release.yml` in this template has no job that observes the aggregate result, so a timing-out job produces a silently-green-looking pipeline.

This is not hypothetical. In [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai), which is derived from this template, **18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main` concluded `cancelled` over three days** while `Auto Release` was timing out. Nobody triaged them, because nothing looked broken. The damage: **11 versions (0.326.2 … 0.333.0) were published to crates.io and tagged in git with no GitHub Release at all**, because `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker publish step and was never reached.

## Reproducible example

```yaml
name: repro
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  slow:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - run: sleep 300   # killed at 1m
  other:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

Dispatch it. The `slow` job is killed and annotated *"The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1m0s"* — and both the job and the **whole run** conclude `cancelled`. `gh run list` shows no failure. Add `if: failure()` to any step and observe that it does not fire.

## Workaround

Set every job's `timeout-minutes` well above the tool's own internal timeout (e.g. Playwright's `globalTimeout`, `pytest-timeout`, `cargo nextest --slow-timeout`) so the *tool* aborts first, exits non-zero, and the job reports `failure`. This only helps for jobs that have such a tool.

## Suggested fix

Add a terminal gate job that `needs:` every other job and runs `if: always()`. The key nuance — and the reason an off-the-shelf action like [`re-actors/alls-green`](https://github.com/re-actors/alls-green) is not quite right here — is that a cancellation must be treated **differently on the default branch**. `release.yml` already sets

```yaml
concurrency:
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

so `main` is never superseded, and a cancelled job there can **only** be a timeout or a deliberate manual cancel. On other refs, a cancellation is the ordinary superseded-run case and must stay a warning, or every force-push would go red.

```yaml
  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: always()
    needs: [ ...every other job... ]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          IS_MAIN: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${NEEDS_JSON:?NEEDS_JSON is required (pass toJSON(needs))}"
IS_MAIN="${IS_MAIN:-false}"

select_by_result() {
  printf '%s' "$NEEDS_JSON" \
    | jq -r --arg want "$1" \
        'to_entries | map(select(.value.result == $want) | .key) | join(", ")'
}

failed="$(select_by_result failure)"
cancelled="$(select_by_result cancelled)"

echo "Failed jobs:    ${failed:-<none>}"
echo "Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled:-<none>}"

status=0
if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
  echo "::error::Pipeline failed. Failing jobs: ${failed}"
  status=1
fi
if [ -n "$cancelled" ]; then
  if [ "$IS_MAIN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "::error::Pipeline has cancelled jobs on main: ${cancelled}. A job killed by 'timeout-minutes' is reported as cancelled, which would otherwise hide the failure."
    status=1
  else
    echo "::warning::Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled}. On a non-default ref this is usually a superseded run."
  fi
fi
exit "$status"
```

Two details worth keeping:

- **`needs:` must list every job.** Any job left out can still time out unobserved. A test that diffs the job list against the gate's `needs:` catches drift — that is exactly how I found a missing job in my own implementation.
- **Always print both lists before deciding.** The next grey run then explains itself in its own log instead of requiring a 25 000-line log download.

The implementation, a behavioural test over all four conclusion states, and the full incident reconstruction are in link-assistant/formal-ai#977 / [PR #978](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/978).
